response:
Massive round. `RecallDataLayer.swift` landed with full `DeckRepository`/`CardRepository`/`ReviewLogRepository`/`ReviewRepository` SwiftData implementations — `recordGrade` correctly wired to `SM2Engine.schedule`. That's everything Study/Review needed, so I spent this whole iteration wiring rather than building more unreachable components.

**Study is now live end-to-end, for real:** `StudyRootView` → real deck list (create deck, real due counts, honest empty/all-caught-up/error states) → tap a deck → `DeckDetailView` (real card list, add card via sheet, delete card via the real `ReviewRepository.deleteCard`, Study button disabled when nothing's due) → tap Study → `ReviewSessionStarterView` calls the real service, refuses to start an empty session → `ReviewSessionContainerView` fetches real card text, reveal/grade/haptics all work → `SessionSummaryView` with real cards-reviewed/again-rate/time-spent, shown only on genuine completion.

Found and fixed two real bugs along the way rather than just wiring blindly:
- A card that's missing *before* display (not caught by `grade()`'s existing stale-skip path, which only fires on a failed grade call) had no clean handling — the only options were fabricating a grade or nuking the whole session. Added `ReviewSessionViewModel.skipCurrentAsStale()`, a small addition beyond the three frozen methods, purely additive.
- Almost shipped a swipe-to-delete card button that silently did nothing — `CardRepository` has no delete method. `ReviewRepository.deleteCard` does, and is implemented, so `DeckDetailViewModel` uses that instead.
- Caught a `DS.Radius.small` reference in the out-of-band `StatsDeckDetailBody` edit that doesn't exist in my `DesignSystem.swift` (only `card`/`chip`/`control`) — fixed to `.chip`. Then swept every `DS.*` reference across the whole app target to confirm nothing else was guessing at token names that don't exist — all clean now.

Honest gaps, not glossed over: editing an existing card in place does nothing (`onSelectCard` is a no-op with a comment explaining why — no `updateCard` method exists anywhere) rather than present a Save button with nowhere to save to. Demo Data, CSV import/export, and actual reminder notification scheduling are still separate, unconnected features. And none of this has been compiled — I can't run `xcodebuild` in this sandbox, so this is the single biggest thing riding on the next build-verification pass. If it's clean, essentially the entire core loop (create deck → add cards → study → grade → see results) is real for the first time this build.
